answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network imposes superlinear stake burning per identity: creating k agents requires destroying k^2 tokens. A genuine validator begins a solitary voyage, anchoring its root state under a resilient willow tree topology where clone graphs cannot mirror legitimate consensus. When malicious actors attempt to mirror identities, cryptographic slashing burns collateral exponentially as O(2^k), making mass spoofing economically ruinous.
